gaps: All 11 model years sourced from hondanews.com (manufacturer); no secondary sources used.
2016 and 2017: LX/Sport/EX manual-transmission versions were cheaper than the recorded CVT rows (see notes); the recorded msrp is the CVT version.
2017 and 2018 hybrid rows come from separate Accord Hybrid pricing releases whose destination charge differs from the gas page of the same year (2017: $875 vs $890; 2018: $890 vs $875).
2019: the source's 'MSRP incl. destination' column has two internal typos (EX, EX-L 2.0T) in both the Jan and Jul 2019 versions; the MSRP column is internally consistent and was used.
2021: three different releases give three destination charges ($955 Oct 2020, $995 Jan 2021, $1,015 Jul 2021) and a $200 MSRP increase in Jan 2021; launch pricing recorded, later prices in notes.
2023: mid-year $550 price cut on EX and all hybrid trims (May 2023); launch pricing recorded.
2026: incl.-destination column for Sport-L and Touring does not reconcile with MSRP + $1,195 on either 2026 page; MSRP column recorded.
Later-dated revisions of the 2018 (5.1.2018), 2020 (7.7.2020), 2022 hybrid (5.03.22) and 2024 (Nov 2023) pricing pages exist on hondanews.com but were not fetched.
